text:
Maya Li: Quick results from overnight kernel sweep on H100 (us-east-1) for redwood-7b-q8. TL;DR: flashattention_v3 gives ~12% tail-p90 improvement and +18% throughput vs triton-default for seq=2048, but one weird regression on token-level ppl for a small subset of prompts.

Eric Thompson: Nice. Can you paste the perf numbers? which q config and batch sizes?

Maya Li: Batch 8, seq 2048, q8_4bit. p50 latency 68ms -> 61ms, p90 210ms -> 184ms, tokens/sec 12.8k -> 15.1k (v2/triton -> v3).

perf-bot: Automated benchmark finished: https://internal.redwood.ai/perf/bench/1765204000 :
- env: redwood-7b-q8, H100 (p4d-like), us-east-1a
- kernels: triton-default vs flashattention_v3
- runs: 3 seeds each, median reported
- artifacts: charts + raw csvs attached to run 1765204000

Sophia Patel: Where's the quality regression? quantify it.

Maya Li: Stumbled on ~0.7% increase in token-level ppl on a 200-prompt eval set (conversational prompts) when using flashv3 with fused rotary kernel. It's not across the board, mostly long-dialog contexts with lots of prefix reuse.

Eric Thompson: Interesting — could be KV-cache difference or numeric accumulation. Did you compare using fp16 vs bf16 runtimes?

Maya Li: Yes, same trend in both. Also tried replicating with A100 (g4dn-family) in eu-west-1: there v3 still wins latency but the ppl delta disappears. So region/GPU shows different numeric behavior.

Sophia Patel: Might be linked to vendor driver/torch-cu version differences. H100 hosts are running 560.xx drivers and cuda 12.x; A100 hosts on 510.xx + cuda 11.8.

Eric Thompson: Can you run minimal reproducer? small prompt that triggers the delta and compare logits between kernels with same seed. use `--dump-logits` so we can diff.

Maya Li: Will run now. Command I used:```./bench/run.sh --model redwood-7b --quant q8_4bit --gpu H100 --kernel flashattention_v3 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --dump-logits ./out/v3.log```and same for `--kernel triton-default` -> `./out/triton.log`

perf-bot: Artifact upload complete: /artifacts/1765204000/v3.log and /artifacts/1765204000/triton.log

Eric Thompson: If logits differ, check rotary/fused-rotary flags and kernel eps / accumulation order. Also try setting `REDWOOD_NUMERIC_SAFE=1` to see if it forces identical reductions.

Maya Li: Ran logits diff: small but consistent deviations after token 512. With `REDWOOD_NUMERIC_SAFE=1` the deviations vanish and ppl matches, but latency regresses to triton levels.

Sophia Patel: So it's a numerical accumulation tradeoff. For throughput/latency wins we get slightly different FP accumulation. We need to decide when to flip default kernel in prod.

Eric Thompson: Proposal: flip default to flashattention_v3 on H100 pools for non-quantized or tolerant workloads, but gate it behind a rollout flag + quality eval for q8 models. Also add region-specific rollouts because A100 vs H100 numeric stack differs.

Maya Li: +1. Also suggest automatic fallback: if quality monitor shows >0.5% ppl regression on a monitored prompt set, revert to triton-default for that customer/route.

Sophia Patel: We'll want an eval job in Redwood Optimize that runs per-customer promptset on kernel changes. I'll add a checklist:
- targeted logits diff reproducer
- run on representative hardware in each region (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1)
- run QPS soak for 1h with production traffic patterns
- add AB test with 5% traffic for 24h and quality gates

Maya Li: I'll open a rollout PR with the kernel toggle env: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=flashattention_v3` and a per-route override. Also adding the numeric-safe opt `REDWOOD_NUMERIC_SAFE` as opt-in.

Eric Thompson: Good. Also record kernel build flags (fused_rotary, block_size) in the model profile so Optimize can recommend kernel per workload.

Sophia Patel: For the record, vendor libs (nvfuser/cuBlas) were also tested — they do fine for some MHA patterns but didn't beat flashv3 on our long-contexts. Keep them as fallback for tiny models.

Maya Li: Plan: run the targeted eval on H100 + A100 in both regions this afternoon, upload diffs, then we can decide toggle strategy by EOD. :hourglass: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Eric Thompson: Thanks — ping us when artifacts are up.

Sophia Patel: Thx Maya. If rollback is tricky, we can do canary with 1 GPU pool using flashv3 and global fallback to triton when quality gate trips.

Maya Li: Will do.
